### Bounded job history and release reliability patch

`v0.2.2` adds lifecycle-aware retention for daemon job history. Active work is
kept unconditionally, routine successes expire after 48 hours by default, and
diagnostically useful failures remain for 14 days. The newest significant
failure per maintenance registration or work stream receives separately bounded
protection, while terminal-job and per-job progress caps remain final safety
limits.

Retention is configurable through validated global service configuration. The
daemon compacts legacy `jobs.json` snapshots on load and prunes on job updates,
completion, and idle reconciliation. The observation API and Admin UI expose the
effective policy, retained counts, oldest retained job, and expiry/truncation
evidence. Expired deep links explicitly explain that cached records, maintenance
frontiers and policy, RAG indexes, and audit receipts are unaffected.

The native GitCode release publisher now verifies assets even when GitCode omits
attachment-size metadata: it performs a bounded byte-count check against the
presigned download URL without forwarding credentials to storage. Publication
also waits for the exact mirrored tag commit before creating a release, removing
a race between the GitHub workflow and GitCode tag visibility.

There are no cache schema migrations or breaking CLI/MCP changes in this patch.
